title: ECHO: Adaptive Community Search over Multimodal Graphs

problem.claim: Community search over multimodal graphs seeks a query-vertex-containing subgraph that is structurally cohesive and semantically coherent with multimodal query inputs.

gap.claim: Existing community search methods do not capture fine-grained multimodal semantics or support effective multimodal fusion.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes ECHO, an adaptive community search framework for multimodal graphs.
ECHO includes a Fine-grained Modality Extractor that decomposes multimodal content into structured local semantic units and operates in an encoder-agnostic manner.

ECHO includes a Dual-Track Mixture of Experts network that separates semantic and structural modeling into parallel tracks and performs adaptive, query-aware feature fusion with a hierarchical MoE architecture.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first study of the community search problem over multimodal graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world multimodal graphs reportedly show that ECHO consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in community quality.
The authors report that ECHO achieves superior search efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies community search over multimodal graphs.
Existing methods are described as insufficient for fine-grained multimodal semantics and multimodal fusion.
ECHO addresses the limitations through a fine-grained modality extractor and a dual-track mixture-of-experts network.
Experiments on real-world multimodal graphs reportedly show improved community quality and search efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates local multimodal semantic extraction from joint semantic-structural feature fusion.

interpretation.claim: Separating representation detail preservation from adaptive fusion may help address both semantic granularity and structural modeling requirements.

application.claim: A multimodal graph-search system could consider dedicated components for fine-grained modality processing and query-aware fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition benefits other multimodal graph tasks or input modalities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative improvements.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, computational costs, or limitations.
